messages:
anna: RFC follow-up — who should own deadline/hedge/fallback decisions: gateway or upstreams? My leaning: gateway should own policy + short-circuiting. Need tradeoffs and compatibility rules.

mike: +1 gateway owned. important: propagate why we hedged so upstreams can attribute cost and adjust throttles (billing/logging). propose header 'x-rw-hedge-reason' + id.

sara: agree gateway owning matches ops model, but we need a strict compatibility manifest per route (kv cache, streaming, seq-len). otherwise fallbacks will break semantics.

ethan: perf note: naive hedging doubles tokens on tail events. suggest soft-hedge: only when p95 > threshold OR sample 1% of requests for continuous monitoring. also need an admission budget.

anna: sketch of proposal: gateway keeps a per-route manifest listing primary & fallback candidates plus compatibility tags. hedge policy = latency threshold + budget + sampling. when gateway hedges it attaches headers so upstreams can annotate logs: 'x-rw-hedge-id', 'x-rw-hedge-cause', 'x-rw-fallback-model'. upstreams can then emit 'hedge.received' metrics.

mike: sample config looks like:

```
route:
  name: chat-gen
  primary: [redwood-v2, open-lima-q8]
  fallbacks: [redwood-v1-quant, open-lima-cpu]
  compatibility: {kv_cache: true, streaming: true, max_seq: 4096}
  hedge:
    enabled: true
    p95_multiplier: 1.5
    budget_per_min: 30
    sample_rate: 0.01
```

sara: streaming handshake is tricky. if primary streams and fallback doesn't, gateway would have to buffer or translate. buffering is risky for long responses. we should require streaming:true for any fallback to allow hedging during streaming endpoints.

ethan: +1. alternative is resumable trailers: let fallback continue from a checkpoint but that requires KV cache alignment which is complex. prefer simple compatibility gating for now.

anna: also: idempotency/side-effect safety. hedging must be forbidden for non-idempotent routes unless route explicitly marks safe. propose header check 'x-rw-idempotent: true' at ingress.

mike: observability: track metrics: hedge.attempts, hedge.successes, hedge.fallback-latency, hedge.token-overhead. also add alert when token-overhead > 10% sustained.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary applied -> route=chat-gen env=staging sha=abc123 :rocket:

ethan: one more operational thought — cost accounting: if fallback is cheaper model, we should tag billing to primary vs fallback and expose breakdown in console. headers + logs enable that.

anna: OK I'll draft a follow-up RFC with: 1) manifest schema, 2) hedge policy semantics, 3) header contract, 4) observability surface, 5) streaming compatibility rules. tagging @sara @mike @ethan for review. :eyes:

mike: lgtm, please include a short microbenchmark plan (p50/p95/p99 with and without hedging)

sara: and a checklist for fallback compatibility tests (kv replay, streaming parity, max_seq).

ethan: and a safety opt-out flag per-team.

anna: thanks — will circulate draft by EOD tomorrow.
